title: the door of the guru
hookLine: the door of the guru; why it's open to anyone
carry: cover your head, take off your shoes, come in

lines: A TALL FLAG ON A POLE.
cards: On a street you know, there's a tall flag, saffron or blue, on a pole outside a building: maybe a white one with domes, maybe a converted warehouse or an old church.
Through the door you can hear singing and drums, and smell something cooking. And someone walking by might wonder: can I just walk in? Today, the answer.

teach.h: GUR, THE GURU. DWARA, A DOOR.
teach.b: Gurdwara. Gur, the Guru. Dwara, a door.

teach.h: OPEN TO ANYONE, FROM EVERY SIDE.
teach.b: The flag from day seven, the Nishan Sahib, is there so it can be found from far away. And yes: anyone can walk in, of any faith or none.
In Amritsar, the Golden Temple was built with doors on all four sides, which Sikhs explain as a welcome from every direction. There are a few things everyone does, Sikh or not.

teach.h: HEAD COVERED, SHOES OFF, HANDS WASHED.
teach.b: Cover your head; gurdwaras usually keep scarves at the door. Take off your shoes. Wash your hands.
Leave tobacco and alcohol outside. That's all.

teach.h: THE WHOLE PATH UNDER ONE ROOF.
teach.b: Inside, the last two weeks meet under one roof. At the front, on a raised platform under a canopy, rests the scripture, the Guru Granth Sahib. People bow, then sit on the floor, all at one level: the sangat.
Musicians sing the hymns: naam japna, out loud. Near the end comes the Ardas, then karah prashad, a warm sweet of flour, butter and sugar, placed in cupped hands. Then the langar.
And the people cooking, cleaning and minding the shoes? That's seva. A gurdwara is the whole path, given a building and a door that stays open.

how: Anyone may visit a gurdwara: visitors cover their heads, remove their shoes and wash their hands, sit on the floor before the Guru Granth Sahib for kirtan, receive karah prashad, and eat in the langar.

games.q: the path, under one roof — tap the pairs.
p: the warm sweet, the same for all

s: you have to be a Sikh to enter a gurdwara

games.q: you're a visitor at a gurdwara door for the first time, and you're not a Sikh. what happens?
o: you're asked to explain your beliefs.
you cover your head, take off your shoes, and come in.
you wait outside until a service ends.
games.why: anyone may come in. head covered, shoes off, hands washed, and a seat on the floor with everyone else.

practice: Do the threshold with your body. Lift your hands to your head, as if laying a cloth over it. Rub your palms together slowly, as if rinsing them.
Feel your feet on the floor, bare or as if they were. Then stay at the door a while, listening: singing somewhere inside, and nobody asking who you are.

wordCard.voice: The gurdwara. The door of the Guru: the Sikh place of worship, open to anyone. Sixteenth word.

orig.note: Punjabi, in Gurmukhi script: gur (the Guru) + duara (door): the door of the Guru.

carryVoice: Your line: cover your head, take off your shoes, come in. That's all a first visit asks of anyone. Day sixteen.
